citation.description: Drain gate in autodeploy.sh: checks bot_in_flight_reviews() and defers if >0

criteria.criterion: A deploy that would interrupt an in-flight review is DEFERRED or DRAINED rather than recreating the container mid-review, proven by a test or a scripted simulation of the busy case.

citation.description: DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX=1800 with rationale; test_defer_bound_default_outlasts_the_apps_own_per_review_cap asserts bound >= DEFAULT_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS

criteria.criterion: The deferral/drain is BOUNDED, so a permanently-busy bot cannot block deploys indefinitely, and the bound is stated with its rationale.

citation.description: AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED marker emitted; observability.sh §4e publishes it as deploy_deferrals CloudWatch metric; test_a_deferred_deploy_is_logged_and_countable verifies

criteria.criterion: A deferred deploy is LOGGED and visible (journald + the autodeploy metric), so a skipped cycle can never be mistaken for no change having landed.

citation.description: rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts CloudWatch alarm watches review_interrupts metric; AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT marker emitted in autodeploy.sh lines 315-325; observability.sh §4e publishes it

criteria.criterion: The interrupted-review failure mode becomes OBSERVABLE: either it emits a countable marker that an alarm can watch, or the gap is explicitly recorded as accepted with its reasoning.

citation.description: test_a_landing_burst_ends_with_the_review_surviving_and_one_deploy: 6 ticks with advancing tips, asserts zero recreations during burst, then exactly one compose-build at newest tip

criteria.criterion: A landing BURST is covered, not just a single deploy: a simulation with commits arriving faster than one review completes ends with the review voting rather than being killed repeatedly.
